rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a promising combination of strong components. Config_032 uses scgpt (RNA) and imagenet_vit_l (image) encoders, which are both high-performing, with transformer aggregation (effective for multiprofile settings) and weighted fusion (a common baseline). This balances exploration of key design choices (encoder strength, aggregation method) while providing a foundation for future exploitation. The expected cost is moderate due to ViT and transformer aggregation, which are more resource-intensive than simpler methods like avgpool.

The existing evidence shows that config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt + imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieved 52% validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 (smaller, cheaper model) while keeping other components the same, to evaluate if a less complex image encoder improves accuracy without increasing cost. It clarifies the impact of image encoder choice on performance, balancing exploration of architectural tradeoffs and cost-efficiency.

Existing evidence shows that config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.5199 validation accuracy with low cost. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation and concat fusion with the same effective image/RNA encoders, clarifying if simpler aggregation/fusion methods could improve accuracy without increasing cost. It balances exploration of aggregation/fusion choices with exploitation of proven encoder combinations.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_032, 0.5199 accuracy) outperforms avgpool with concat fusion (config_005, 0.5176 accuracy). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with concat fusion to clarify whether fusion method or aggregation type drives performance. It is a low-cost (estimated 2.86 GPU hours) logical extension of the current top-performing configuration, balancing exploration of critical design choices while maintaining budget efficiency.

Existing evidence shows config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.5199). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 while retaining the high-performing imagenet_vit_l image encoder and avgpool aggregation. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice is critical for performance, balancing exploration of representation methods with cost efficiency. Expected cost: ~5-7 GPU hours, preserving budget flexibility for future experiments.

The existing evidence shows that using pca_n2000 RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (as in config_048) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l (used in config_048) with resnet50 (a less expensive model) maintains similar performance while reducing training cost. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of cost-effective alternatives.

Existing evidence shows that using pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_051) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with concat fusion to evaluate if the fusion method significantly impacts performance. It clarifies the importance of fusion strategy while maintaining cost efficiency (estimated 7.0 GPU hours), balancing exploitation of current top performers with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image encoders with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_051) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests a logical extension by replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could potentially improve performance. While more expensive than previous experiments, it clarifies whether advanced aggregation methods can further enhance accuracy without sacrificing too much cost. This balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of new methods.

The existing evidence shows config_051 (0.639 accuracy) and config_048 (0.635 accuracy) are top performers using pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image encoders. This experiment tests a similar RNA/image encoder pair (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image) with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could potentially improve accuracy by exploring a different aggregation method. The expected cost is ~6.76 GPU hours (similar to config_028), balancing exploration of aggregation methods while staying within budget.

Existing evidence shows config_050 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.6878). This experiment tests changing fusion from concat to weighted with the same RNA/image encoders and transformer aggregation, which could further improve accuracy. The configuration is similar to the current best but with a different fusion method, offering a low-cost (estimated ~5 GPU hours) way to explore a key design choice with minimal additional cost.
